decision: Kind of hand-off (crew work / owner enforcement / referral elsewhere) is read from N2's final rule column, with four phrase overrides: "vehicle not derelict, refer to treasurer for ticketing" and "sent to parking enforcement" are owner enforcement; "referred to proper department" and "building was occupied, will need police" are referral elsewhere.
why: R-COMMON asks for the three kinds throughout; N2's rules (build/N2/closure_class.sql) already separate enforcement and external agencies, and the four overrides are phrases whose rule label (internal_referral / external_agency) does not match who must act.
alternative_rejected: Hand-classifying all 134 hand-off phrases afresh: slower and not reproducible from N2's reviewed table.

decision: Referrals to another city crew (forestry, water division, street maintenance, refuse, parks) count as crew work, not referral elsewhere.
why: R-COMMON defines crew work as "the city will do it"; referral elsewhere is MSD, Ameren or another agency outside the city.
alternative_rejected: Counting every internal referral as referral elsewhere, which would move about 6,700 closures out of crew work.

decision: "Vehicle tagged for tow" is crew work (the tow), although the tag itself is a notice to the vehicle owner.
why: R-COMMON lists tow among crew work. No public tow record exists either way, so the choice moves 3,072 closures between kinds but changes no traced figure.

decision: Weeds are graded on 2026 filings only. 2025 vacant-lot requests are excluded; 2025 vacant-building requests are shown only as a sensitivity row.
why: The 2025 ledger is thin for Grass Maint (4,052 distinct cuts in 2025 vs 31,527 in 2026 and 38,850 in 2024; N1 reported the same), while Weed-Grass, the vacant-building cut, looks complete in 2025 (8,182 vs 8,369 in 2026).
alternative_rejected: Pooling 2025 and 2026, which would count missing 2025 ledger entries as undone work.

decision: "Done" means the first recorded work on or after the filing date, compared with the request's own PRJCOMPLETEDATE; strict comparison, with a +7-day sensitivity.
why: The promise is the city's own (COMMON 1); ledger dates are weekly posting batches, so a cut can be posted up to a week after it happened.
alternative_rejected: CityStat goals or our own guess at a reasonable time.

decision: "No record" is counted only where the promise passed on or before 13 Sep 2026; the headline denominator is restricted to those requests so that done by promise, late and no record add to 100%.
why: R-COMMON: count "never done" only where the promise passed at least 30 days before 13 Oct 2026.
alternative_rejected: Including requests whose promise is still recent, which would mix "not yet" with "never".

decision: Board-ups are joined on the layer's ParcelID to N1's request parcel, or on the normalised address (N1 normaliser).
why: The layer carries ParcelID; N2 joined on address only. Either key counts as a match.
alternative_rejected: Address only (N2), which misses spelling variants.

decision: DateBoardedUp is read as a UTC calendar date.
why: The field holds midnight UTC (e.g. 1560384000000 = 2019-06-13T00:00Z); converting to Central would move every board-up back a day.

decision: Weeds baseline: each requested parcel-date is compared with the mean of its same-block rotation controls (ledger CITYBLOCK; cut at least once in 2026; no weed request in the 60 days to the date), request-weighted; plus a like-for-like variant (requested parcels also on the rotation) and an other-block, same-ward variant.
why: The brief's design. Request weighting stops big blocks dominating. The like-for-like variant removes the fact that controls are on the rotation by construction. The other-block variant tests whether a request moves the whole block.
alternative_rejected: Pooling control parcels, and comparing the parcel with itself on other dates (not done for time).

decision: Tree work orders are graded as partial. A converted request matched to an open order in Cityworks saved search 6955 counts as still open; an unmatched one is unknown.
why: The sample holds only open (NEW) orders, so it can show "still open" but never "done". Its ids rise with start date (r = 0.997, newest 8 Jan 2026), so it looks complete for older orders (inferred).

decision: LRA demolition is kept out of the headline.
why: Only one LRA demolition request was closed at a hand-off in 2025-26; the city keeps these open (190 open). The open ones are reported as "open but already demolished" instead.

decision: CityStat restatement uses N4's definition C. "Hand-offs not counted" = on-time share x (1 - hand-off share of on-time closures); "only done" = on-time and done / all closed. The denominator stays CityStat's.
why: Definition C reproduces CityStat (N4). Keeping the denominator shows the same requests the city counts, scored only by what their closing words say.
alternative_rejected: Dropping hand-offs from the denominator too, which would hide them.

decision: Re-reports after done vs hand-off closures are cited from R2's file (build/R2/rereport_type_compare.csv), not recomputed.
why: R1 brief: R2 does the full re-report table; coordinate via files, do not duplicate.

decision: Request-level outcomes (with request ids) are written only to build/R1/private/; every other R1 output is aggregated by service, phrase, ward group or quarter.
why: COMMON 10 and Jack's ruling: no ids and nothing below block level in public outputs.

decision: Kept-open requests are compared with closed-at-hand-off ones and the result is reported even though it cuts against the entry: open requests have far less recorded work.
why: Brief: say plainly if the data cut against us. The confound (open = stalled at inspection or owner notice) is stated beside it.

decision: The headline keeps R-COMMON's rule (promise passed at least 30 days before 13 Oct) and is shown beside a stricter version (promise at least three months old: 16.2% done by promise, 61.0% late, 22.8% no record).
why: No-record shares fall as promises age: board-ups 62% at 30-60 days to 14.8% at three months or more; weeds 49.5% to 36.5%. Part of "no record" at 30 days is very late work not yet done or recorded.
alternative_rejected: Reporting only the 30-day version, which overstates "never" for board-ups.

decision: Board-up "no record" is reported as not evidence of lost work, because the board-up layer's recall on buildings 311 says the city secured is 80.6% (54 of 67; 95% CI 69.6-88.3%).
why: A record that misses about one board-up in five cannot show that 18% of referrals were never boarded. Weed "no record" survives the same tests: it is 36.5% three months on; 91% of no-record vacant lots appear in the ledger in other years; and the ledger holds more cuts than CityStat publishes for the same weeks (T-COMMON: 7,545 vs 7,099 parcels).
alternative_rejected: Treating every missing record as undone work.

decision: Give R2 a measured range rather than a single rate: never done 14.8% (board-ups, three months on, raw) to 36.5% (weeds, three months on); late 44.7% (weed lots) to 64.6% (board-ups).
why: The two traced services differ in kind (rotation mowing vs a dispatched crew); the range brackets them, and the low end is flagged as indistinguishable from zero after record recall.
alternative_rejected: The pooled 32.2%, which mixes a robust weeds figure with a board-up figure within record error.
